note.corpus: The cases named m_<path>_<candidate>_<approver> are the enrolment matrix: every combination of authoriser path (lan, an authorization object; phone, an ORI-ENROL-V1 text), candidate kind (lan, sms) and candidate approver (minted, own, other). The cases named e_<path>_<condition> are the authoriser eligibility block: every combination of authoriser path (lan, phone) and authoriser condition (absent, not_active, wrong_kind, not_preexisting, eligible). The cases named x_<table>_<row>_<axes> are the refusal sweep, each decided by its row: steps (the Order-of-refusal steps) over every registry operation, and over evidence_commission for payload_too_large and invalid_arguments; cp (Challenges presented) over recover, and over local_seed (a lan challenge) and enrol (a lan or sms challenge) each x presented candidate kind (lan, sms, whatsapp), a presented kind other than the challenge's being decided at candidate_changed unless an earlier row fires; challenge_unavailable over the presented candidate kind alone, no challenge being held, and device_binding_mismatch and site_binding_mismatch also with no challenge held, over recover and the presented kind for local_seed and enrol; an expired sms challenge sitting between the 60-second challenge window and the 10-minute possession window; ch (Challenge) for an enrolment over candidate kind (lan, sms) x request approver (null, named), except phone_pending_for_value (sms only), channel_unauthenticated (whatsapp, and sms while the runtime has no authenticated SMS ingress) and approver_revoked and approver_unknown (named only); rc, ls, rv and bd (Recover, Local seed, Revoke, Binding) alone; en (Enrol) over authoriser path (lan, phone) x candidate kind (lan, sms), and from challenge_stale on, where the registry is held, also x candidate approver (minted, own, and other up to authorizer_not_approver; registry_unavailable has no approver axis), except that signature_invalid_authorization is lan-path only, possession_invalid and signature_invalid_possession are lan-candidate only, phone_pending_for_value is sms-candidate only, authorizer_not_approver is other only and approver_revoked minted only; ms (member strictness) over member form (escaped_duplicate, case_variant, unknown_member) x location (top, candidate, authorization, possession, document), malformed inside a document and invalid_arguments elsewhere. Each case is one request on the operator socket and the runtime's answer to it under the context given. Every case is independent; contexts do not carry over. A replay sends `request` as its UTF-8 bytes followed by one LF, from a peer with the context's credentials, and compares the answer with `expected`.
note.request: The exact bytes the client sends, as UTF-8 text; `request_bytes` is their length in UTF-8 bytes. The runtime reads the bytes before the first LF, so a request that holds an LF is judged on the bytes before it and the bound is compared with their length.
note.terminated: true: the client sends one LF after `request`. false: the connection ends after `request` with no further byte, so a request that holds no LF ends before any LF.
note.signatures: A signed object is a possession (verified under the candidate's value at Local seed's or Enrol's possession signature_invalid row), an authorization (under the named active credential's value, at Enrol's first signature_invalid row) or a revocation document (under its signing_key, at Revoke's signature_invalid row). A case may carry a signed object whose signature does not verify only when its answer is decided by a step of Order of refusal, by a row of Challenges presented, or by a row of the operation's table that comes before that object's signature row or is that row. In every other case each signed object the request carries verifies under its key.
note.expected.changes: Every state change the answer commits, sorted, from this closed vocabulary: challenge_added:<challenge_id> (a pending challenge with its deadline); code_sent:<challenge_id> (a possession code sent to the challenge's phone candidate); used:<challenge_id> (the challenge marked used); registry_created:<identity_epoch> (an empty initialized registry under that epoch, the context's device_id and the verified site: revision 1, last external revision 0, credential sequence 0, no credentials or tombstones); challenges_cleared, phone_authorizations_cleared and pending_phone_cleared (every held challenge, received phone authorization and pending phone operation removed); credential_added:<credential_id> (the candidate made active); sequence:<n> and revision:<n> (the new credential sequence and registry revision); pending_phone_added:<value> (a pending phone operation for the candidate); credential_tombstoned:<credential_id> and value_tombstoned:<value> (an active credential removed, its ID and value tombstoned); approver_tombstoned:<approver_id>; and last_external_revision:<n>. A refusal lists [] or, when it consumes its challenge, only used:<challenge_id>. Every successful recover lists challenges_cleared, phone_authorizations_cleared and pending_phone_cleared, whether or not anything was held, and still lists used:<challenge_id> for the challenge it consumes and clears in the same transaction. registry_created implies revision 1, last external revision 0 and credential sequence 0, which are not listed separately. The recorded fingerprint of the last applied revocation document changes with last_external_revision and has no token of its own.
note.context.keys_failing_admission: The configured anchors' keys and active lan_ed25519 credential keys (canonical Base64 of the raw 32 bytes) that this fixture deliberately holds although they fail ed25519-key-admission/v1. Every other key in the context passes it.
note.context.device_id: The running runtime's device identity. An initialized registry whose device_id differs from it is bound to another device.
note.context.verified_site_id: The device.site_id of the runtime's verified provisioning configuration.
note.context.peer_uid: The peer's effective user ID from kernel peer credentials; null when they cannot be established.
note.context.operator_uid: The installed operator identity; null when none is installed.
note.context.registry_operation_in_flight: Whether another admitted registry operation is in flight.
note.context.anchor_available: Whether the current provisioning anchor is present and usable.
note.context.anchors: The configured anchors' raw Ed25519 public keys, canonical Base64: the current provisioning anchor, the previous provisioning anchor, and one anchor of another class.
note.context.registry: null when the registry is locked. Otherwise its device binding, site binding, identity epoch, registry revision, last external revision, the SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the Profile 2 canonical JSON of the last applied revocation document or null, credential sequence, active credentials (each with its approver ID, credential ID, channel, value as in a challenge candidate, and enrolment sequence), the credentials tombstoned in this epoch (each with its credential ID and the approver ID it belonged to), the approver IDs tombstoned in this epoch, and the values tombstoned in this epoch: revoking a credential tombstones its value as well as its ID.
note.context.challenges: Challenges the runtime holds, each with its challenge object, its state (pending; used, already presented; or expired, its deadline passed and not yet presented), the registry's credential sequence when it was created, and elapsed_ms, the monotonic milliseconds since it was created. A challenge not used is expired exactly when elapsed_ms exceeds 60,000, the challenge window, whatever its candidate's channel; the separate 10-minute phone possession window never extends it. A challenge absent from the list is one the runtime does not hold.
note.context.phone_authorizations: ORI-ENROL-V1 texts the runtime has received and attributed through a phone channel's authenticated ingress, in the order they arrived: the challenge ID and challenge SHA-256 the text carries, and the credential ID of the sender. The first entry for a challenge ID is that challenge's authorization, whoever its sender; a later entry for the same challenge ID is ignored. A sender the runtime could not attribute to a credential is represented by a credential ID that is neither active nor tombstoned.
note.context.pending_phone_values: Phone values with a pending phone operation, on either phone channel.
note.context.authenticated_phone_channels: The phone channels that have an authenticated ingress at the runtime. In v1 only sms can; an empty list means the runtime has no authenticated SMS ingress, so an sms candidate is channel_unauthenticated. The set is fixed for a run, so a held challenge whose candidate is on a phone channel the list leaves out is not a valid context.
note.context.minted: The values the runtime's CSPRNG yields for the next challenge: challenge ID, approver ID, credential ID, and the prospective identity epoch for a recover challenge. null unless the request is a well-formed challenge request that reaches the Challenge table.
note.expected: ok true with the exact `result` object, or ok false with the `error.code`. `consumes_challenge` appears for the operations that present a challenge: whether the named challenge is used afterwards because of this request. A refusal changes nothing else.
note.keys: Ed25519 private keys are SHA-256 of 'ori operator-socket/v3 <label> test key'; challenge_sha256 is SHA-256 of the challenge's Profile 2 canonical JSON. Test keys only.
